sections.title: Adjectives: Describing People & Things
sections.instructions: Choose the correct adjective from Unit 9. Think about meaning and feeling.

questions.sentence: The party was very loud — the music was so ___.
questions.explanation: 'Noisy' means making a lot of noise — loud and unpleasant.

questions.sentence: Our superhero is on the page by himself. He is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Alone' means by yourself, with no other people around.

questions.sentence: The dragon was so big! It had a ___ mouth and sharp teeth.
questions.explanation: 'Huge' means very, very big.

questions.sentence: The man wore a tall hat and a long, dark coat. He looked very ___.
questions.explanation: 'Strange' means unusual or different in a way that surprises you.

questions.sentence: His dog was small and not very nice. It was a ___, little dog.
questions.explanation: 'Horrible' means very unpleasant or bad.

questions.sentence: The puppy is small. It's a ___, sweet thing.
questions.explanation: 'Little' means small in size.

questions.sentence: He found a £20 note in the street. He is so ___ today!
questions.explanation: 'Lucky' means good things happen to you by chance.

questions.sentence: She got 100% in the maths test. Her result is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Excellent' means very, very good.

questions.sentence: The hero has ___ shoes that help him jump higher than anyone else.
questions.explanation: 'Special' means different in a good way — not ordinary.

questions.sentence: The cinema was full. There weren't any ___ seats left.
questions.explanation: 'Spare' means extra or free — none were left.

questions.sentence: I'm reading a really ___ book — I can't put it down!
questions.explanation: Something you want to keep reading is interesting.

questions.sentence: That film was so ___. I almost fell asleep.
questions.explanation: If a film makes you sleepy, it's boring.

questions.sentence: Rollercoasters are really ___ — my heart was racing!
questions.explanation: An exciting thing makes you feel full of energy and happy.

questions.sentence: The horror film was so ___ that I had to close my eyes.
questions.explanation: Something that makes you afraid is frightening.

questions.sentence: I was very ___ when I got an unexpected present from my best friend.
questions.explanation: 'Surprised' means you didn't expect what happened.

sections.title: Before, After & When Clauses
sections.instructions: Choose the correct linking word: before, after or when. Think about the order of events.

questions.sentence: I always wash my hands ___ I eat dinner.
questions.explanation: Washing hands happens first, then eating — so 'before'.

questions.sentence: ___ we got home, we made some tea.
questions.explanation: Getting home happens first, then making tea — so 'after'.

questions.sentence: I'll call you ___ I arrive at the station.
questions.explanation: 'When' means at the moment something happens.

questions.sentence: Rose got really wet ___ I gave her my umbrella (it was already raining).
questions.explanation: From the textbook example — Rose got wet before getting the umbrella.

questions.sentence: He ran really fast ___ Fred came out of the trees (Fred came out first).
questions.explanation: 'When' marks the moment Fred came out — and Fred running was at that moment.

questions.sentence: ___ we met Grandma's sister in China, we ate the fantastic noodles.
questions.explanation: First they met Grandma's sister, then they ate noodles.

questions.sentence: Last month we 'got' coming in the forest. We took a boat ride on the lake ___ we had a windsurfing lesson.
questions.explanation: First the boat ride, then the lesson — 'before' the lesson.

questions.sentence: Our first trip was to the funfair. ___ we got off, we got on one of the rides, we 'bought' this amazing photo.
questions.explanation: First they got off, then they bought the photo.

questions.sentence: I clean my teeth ___ I go to bed every night.
questions.explanation: Cleaning teeth happens first, then sleep — 'before'.

questions.sentence: We had pancakes ___ we got back from the walk.
questions.explanation: The walk happened first, then pancakes.

questions.sentence: Call me ___ you're ready and I'll come to pick you up.
questions.explanation: 'When' = at the moment that you're ready.

questions.sentence: I always check the weather ___ I go out.
questions.explanation: Check happens first, then go out.

questions.sentence: ___ I was four years old, I lived in Spain.
questions.explanation: 'When I was ...' = at that time in my life.

questions.sentence: We had dinner ___ visited the museum.
questions.explanation: (Dinner happened after the museum visit.)

questions.sentence: He played football ___ he did his homework (homework was after football).
questions.explanation: Football happened first → 'before' homework.

sections.title: -ed / -ing Adjective Endings
sections.instructions: Choose the correct adjective ending. -ed describes how a person feels. -ing describes the thing or activity that causes the feeling.

questions.sentence: I'm so ___ — I've been hiking all day.
questions.explanation: 'Tired' describes how a person feels (the result).

questions.sentence: Hiking up the mountain was really ___.
questions.explanation: 'Tiring' describes the activity that makes you tired.

questions.sentence: I think going to a museum is ___ — I love learning about history.
questions.explanation: The museum is the thing that causes interest → 'interesting'.

questions.sentence: She was ___ in the painting at the museum.
questions.explanation: She is the person who feels interest → 'interested'.

questions.sentence: That ride is so ___ — I want to go on it again!
questions.explanation: The ride causes the feeling → 'exciting'.

questions.sentence: The children were really ___ about the school trip.
questions.explanation: The children feel excitement → 'excited'.

questions.sentence: Maths homework is so ___! I keep falling asleep.
questions.explanation: The homework is the cause → 'boring'.

questions.sentence: Jay was ___ because there was nothing to do.
questions.explanation: The person feels boredom → 'bored'.

questions.sentence: The dark forest at night looked ___.
questions.explanation: The forest is the cause of fear → 'frightening'.

questions.sentence: I was ___ when I heard a strange noise outside my window.
questions.explanation: The person feels fear → 'frightened'.

questions.sentence: Getting a surprise present made me feel really ___.
questions.explanation: The person feels the emotion → 'surprised'.

questions.sentence: The ending of the book was really ___ — I didn't expect it!
questions.explanation: The book caused the feeling → 'surprising'.

questions.sentence: Yes, it is going to be ___ (the activity will make you tired).
questions.explanation: From the Grammar Spotlight: 'Yes, it is going to be tiring.'

questions.sentence: You're going to be ___ at the end of your holiday.
questions.explanation: From the Grammar Spotlight: 'You're going to be tired ...'

questions.sentence: Camping in the mountains was ___ — we had so much fun!
questions.explanation: The activity caused excitement → '-ing' form.

sections.title: Compass Directions (Hiking)
sections.instructions: Choose the correct compass direction. North, south, east and west are the main directions on a map.

questions.sentence: The opposite of north is ___.
questions.explanation: On a compass, north and south are opposites.

questions.sentence: The opposite of east is ___.
questions.explanation: On a compass, east and west are opposites.

questions.sentence: The sun rises in the ___.
questions.explanation: The sun always rises in the east.

questions.sentence: The sun sets in the ___.
questions.explanation: The sun always sets in the west.

questions.sentence: If your compass needle points up the map (top), you are facing ___.
questions.explanation: On most maps, north is at the top.

questions.sentence: Jasmin's family used the ___ to find their way when they didn't have a compass.
questions.explanation: From Jasmin's diary: 'We looked back at the hotel … noticed the stars were not very bright.'

questions.sentence: Before hiking, you should put a ___ in your rucksack.
questions.explanation: A compass is essential for finding your way when hiking.

questions.sentence: You should also pack a ___ in case it gets dark.
questions.explanation: A torch lets you see in the dark — useful for hiking.

questions.sentence: Always take a ___ so you don't get lost. It shows you the way.
questions.explanation: From the textbook: 'When you go hiking, you should take a map so you don't get lost.'

questions.sentence: North, ___ , east and west are the four main compass directions.
questions.explanation: The four main compass directions are N, S, E, W.

sections.title: Reading: A Letter from Summer Camp
sections.instructions: Read the letter from summer camp, then answer the questions.
sections.passage:
Hi William!

How are you? I was so happy to hear from you. I'm so excited! I'm going to go to the beach with my family tomorrow. We wanted to go camping but my brother said he was worried about sleeping in a tent. My parents said we could go to a hotel. My parents are pleased because my rucksack is packed! But they are worried because my sister's suitcase is huge!

When we arrive, we're going to go on a tour of the museum. I think museums are interesting, but my brother feels bored. He wants to build sandcastles. Where are you going to go on your holiday? If you come to my country, please write and tell me.

Love, Nicola

P.S. Before we leave, I'm going to buy a new camera. After the holiday, I'll send you lots of photos! The trip is going to be tiring but exciting.

questions.answer: Her brother was worried about sleeping in a tent

sections.title: Reading: Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl
sections.instructions: Read the legend of Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl, then answer the questions.
sections.passage:
Long, long ago, there was a beautiful princess called Iztaccihuatl. Popocatepetl was a young warrior. He was in love with the beautiful princess and she was in love with him too. But before they could get married, Popocatepetl had to go to war to fight against dangerous tribes who attacked their land. The leader of Popocatepetl's tribe spoke to him.

'We need you to help me with the beautiful princess. We will help you marry my daughter,' he said.

Popocatepetl had to say goodbye to Iztaccihuatl, and go and fight.

Iztaccihuatl was lonely and sad. One day she heard that Popocatepetl was dead. She became very ill. In the end, she died of a broken heart.

But Popocatepetl wasn't dead. Very soon, he returned. When he discovered that Iztaccihuatl was dead, he picked up her body in his arms and carried her away. He laid her down on the ground in a quiet place, and sat down next to her. Snow fell and covered their two bodies.

The gods stopped and pointed up at the two mountains in front of them. 'Look! Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl are still there! They are the two volcanoes.'

Harry and Sophie were on holiday in Mexico with their cousins, Jaime and Alicia. Before they went hiking, they tried to climb Popocatepetl. Popocatepetl is a volcano not very far from Mexico City. The night before the climb, they camped at the bottom of the mountain with their mountain climbing guide, Harry and Jaime looked up at the volcano covered with snow.

'It's going to be exciting tomorrow!' said Jaime. Harry was excited too. 'What a strange shape that mountain is,' said Sophie suddenly. 'It looks like a woman lying down.'

The guide looked where she was pointing. 'Yes,' he said. 'It does. That's a volcano too. Let's put up the tents before it gets dark, and then I can tell you the story of the two volcanoes.'
